profile.campus: Aurora, Kane/DuPage County, Illinois (CyrusOne CHI1 building)
profile.reading:
Per a Baxtel listing dedicated to this exact facility name, corroborated by a datacentermap CHI1 listing and SEC filing language referring to a "Chicago-Aurora I" data center, this building sits at 2905 Diehl Road, Aurora, IL, part of the shared 450,000 sq ft / 114MW CHI1-CHI3 campus.

This is CyrusOne's original Aurora, Illinois facility, purchased from CME Group (the Chicago Mercantile Exchange's parent) in March 2016 for roughly $130 million, with CME Group continuing to operate its Globex electronic-trading matching engine on site under a 15-year lease, per Wikipedia's CyrusOne entry; CyrusOne was founded in July 2000 by David Ferdman and Larry Bursten and was taken private in 2022 when Kohlberg Kravis Roberts (KKR) and Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP) acquired the company for approximately $15 billion.

Since going private under KKR and GIP ownership in 2022, CyrusOne has continued expanding its US and international footprint; the company's own press materials cite roughly $1 billion in cumulative capital investment in its San Antonio, Texas campuses alone as of a January 2025 groundbreaking, indicating continued growth investment across its portfolio under private ownership rather than a broad slowdown following the take-private transaction.

In November 2021, KKR and GIP first announced the agreement to acquire CyrusOne in an approximately $15 billion transaction, one of the largest data center M&A deals of that period, reflecting broader private-equity and infrastructure-fund interest in colocation real estate that has also driven acquisitions of peers like QTS (by Blackstone) and CoreSite (by American Tower) around the same era; CyrusOne's current published portfolio language describes more than 50 mission-critical facilities worldwide, though the company's own site and Wikipedia give somewhat different approximate totals (over 40 versus more than 50), neither of which this registry treats as a precise, independently verified figure.

reading.body:
CyrusOne Chicago Aurora CME occupies 450,000 square feet on Diehl Road in Aurora, Illinois. The operator publishes 114 MW of total IT capacity across a three-building Aurora campus, though the published specifications do not confirm what portion belongs to this specific facility. The campus was purchased from CME Group in 2016 and continues to host CME's Globex matching engine under a lease agreement.

Illinois has 44 mapped data center facilities total, of which six publish power specifications aggregating to 236 MW. This Aurora campus ranks seventh among published facilities in the state by capacity. The unpublished portion of Illinois's data center footprint is therefore substantial relative to what operators have disclosed.

At typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, 114 MW would support approximately 2,850 racks across the three-building campus as a whole. The campus qualifies to host financial market infrastructure, but the operator's published specifications do not declare which tenants currently occupy space or what portion of capacity remains available for expansion.
